llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed Typecho blog manager, but its broad activation wording and direct publish/delete authority make accidental public changes plausible.

dimensions.detail: The CLI capabilities to list, read, create, update, and delete Typecho posts match the stated blog-management purpose, including use of a configured Typecho API token.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The activation language includes broad phrases such as writing notes, knowledge base, Typecho, and my blog, while the skill can publish, update, and delete posts; this is under-scoped for public content mutation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package declares a local typecho-cli binary and no hidden installer, package manager step, or unrelated executable behavior was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Reading TYPECHO_DOMAIN, TYPECHO_TOKEN, and a local config file is expected for this integration, and the token is only used as the Authorization header to the configured blog endpoint.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill defaults new posts to public publish, stores long-lived credentials in a user config path, and supports irreversible deletion; the written instructions require delete confirmation, but the CLI itself has no confirmation interlock.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you want an agent to manage a real Typecho blog. Use it with explicit commands for publish, update, and delete, keep the API token limited and rotated, and confirm the exact post cid before any deletion or full-text update.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] unexpected: The broad trigger wording is artifact-backed and materially increases risk because the same skill can perform public write and delete operations, even though those operations are part of its stated purpose.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The delete command immediately sends a delete action for a cid with no CLI-level prompt or force flag; the skill text says to do a second confirmation, which reduces but does not remove the concern.
[E2] expected: Access to TYPECHO_TOKEN is expected for a Typecho API client and the artifact does not show credential harvesting or transmission to an unrelated destination.
